lede: Wall Street had its best day since April and Asian stocks followed as oil slid on hopes of a US–Iran de-escalation, while the dollar gave back part of Friday's payroll gains. Markets now price roughly an 85% chance of a December Fed hike going into today's October CPI report at 16:30 TRT.
snapshot_time: Gold ≈03:30 TRT · FX/Brent Asia session ≈03:00 TRT · US500 = Mon close

focus.text: Gained about 1.4–1.7% Monday as falling oil eased inflation worries; now just under $4,130, above its 4,112.0 pivot. Main risk: US CPI at 16:30 TRT.
Jumped about 0.7% Monday as the oil slump and equity rally knocked the dollar; holding near 1.1220, mid-range of 1.1103–1.1272. Main risk: US CPI at 16:30 TRT.

technicals.note: Monday's rally lifted gold to its highest since 21 October; price is back under the 4,145–4,157 band that capped last week's rebound.

technicals.indicators: Intraday bias neutral · below 55-day EMA ≈ 1.1323 · longer-term risk lower while 1.1710 caps
technicals.note: Monday's rebound erased most of Friday's drop and put the pair back in the middle of its 1.1103–1.1272 consolidation band.

technicals.indicators: 2H RSI recovered from below 30 · upside favoured while 1.3271 holds
technicals.note: Cable is recovering inside the pullback from last week's 1.3502 high, supported by a rising trendline near 1.33.
Bitcoin is stuck in a tight $73.6k–75.5k band after the weekend flush; analysts flag a lower shelf at $71.3k–67.9k if 73.7k gives way.

news.text: S&P 500 rose 2.35% to 7,549.94, its biggest gain since April; Nasdaq +2.7% as chipmakers rebounded even with Nvidia down on a board probe.
Brent slid toward $91.5, its lowest since early September, after Trump said he would hold off on new strikes on Iran; analysts warn talks remain fragile.
Futures imply about an 85% chance of a December hike after strong October payrolls; economists expect October CPI at 3.9% y/y, core 2.8%.
Kospi surged over 5%, triggering a circuit breaker, and the Nikkei gained around 3% as tech shares bounced.
US yields stayed elevated, with the 10-year near 4.87% and the 2-year around 4.56%, keeping a lid on gold's rebound.
Crypto sat out Monday's equity rally: bitcoin stayed below $75,000 while the Nasdaq gained nearly 3%.
US spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $1.28B last week, the most since June, and ether funds about $365M.
Avalanche gained roughly 6–8% after an NYSE-affiliated unit said it plans a tokenized-securities platform using Avalanche as its core ledger.
Qivalis, a group of 37 European banks, won Dutch authorisation to issue a euro stablecoin; the UK FCA opened crypto applications for banks.
Binance promised an independent review after reports that North Korea-linked hackers used NEAR memecoins to disguise stolen funds as trading profit.
MSCI's final list of index-exclusion candidates, including Strategy (MSTR), is due Wednesday with BTC near Strategy's average cost.

upcoming.note: Exp 0.3% m/m (prev 0.6%), 3.9% y/y (prev 3.7%); core exp 2.8% y/y
